name: 7-Zip RT
author: hamed7ir
description: 7-Zip RT is 7-Zip 26.06 for old ARM Windows tablets: the Surface RT on Windows RT 8.1 and the Surface 2 on Windows 10 ARM32, with one file for both. It's my unofficial fork of 7-Zip by Igor Pavlov, and he doesn't make or support it. It's a native ARM32 (Thumb-2) build with PGO and ThinLTO, profiled on a real Surface 2. It has a dark theme in Kodi RT purple, or a light one, and you can pick another colour: the toolbar, the program icon and the archive file icons follow it. The Explorer context menu works on Windows RT, because it's registered only for your user. It has its own settings and its own menu, so it never mixes with an official 7-Zip. Once a day it checks GitHub for a newer 7-Zip RT and offers to install it, and you can turn that off. 7-Zip's translations are included.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.0 or newer, only for the installer. Windows RT 8.1 and Windows 10 already have it. 7-Zip RT itself needs nothing.
instructionSteps: On Windows RT, jailbreak the device first. RT only runs unsigned desktop apps after a jailbreak.

Run 7-Zip-RT-Setup-26.06-arm32.exe. It installs only for your user (to %LocalAppData%\Programs\7-Zip RT) and doesn't need admin. In the setup you pick your colour, and whether you want the context menu, Open with and a desktop shortcut.
The files are not signed, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.

If you also have the official 7-Zip, both context menus show up in Explorer. With UAC turned off, or on the built-in Administrator account, Windows ignores per-user context menus, so there the setup registers the menu for all users.

7-Zip RT checks GitHub once a day for a newer version. Update now downloads the new setup, checks its SHA-256 and runs it, and your choices and settings stay. Help > Check for updates checks right away, and Options > Settings turns the daily check off.
To remove it, use Control Panel or Settings > Apps.
